text: It may be objected that the chapter merely follows the economy of ancient narrative, which rarely reports the feelings of its persons, and never explains either feeling or motive; and the objection may be in part just. But the narrator of Genesis can report feeling when he will: Esau cries out, Jacob is afraid, Joseph weeps. The reticence of chapter 22 is deliberate; the narrator knows his own reserve, and Restraint here accuses because Genesis 22 withholds feeling.
